references.text: Sarah bore Isaac to Abraham in his old age, as God had promised – this is what the servant recounts in 24:36.
Abraham gave all he owned to Isaac, a direct parallel to the servant's words that Abraham has given his son everything he owns.
Abraham was one hundred years old when the promise concerning Isaac was given, which underscores 'in her old age' in the verse.
The Epistle to the Hebrews mentions Sarah as an example of faith – she bore a son despite her old age, in accordance with God's promise.
Sarah and Abraham were old, and Sarah laughed at the thought of having a child – background for the expression 'in her old age'.
Describes the same event from different perspectives: prophetic fulfillment (21:2) and historical summary (24:36).
Fulfillment of prophecy: 24:36 confirms that the 'difficult' promise in 18:14 was fulfilled.
Connects the event (24:36) to its cause: God's faithfulness in fulfilling the promise (21:1).
Sarah's own confirmation of the event that the servant refers to in 24:36.
Theological interpretation: 11:11 explains the role of faith in the event reported in 24:36.
Contrast between doubt about age (18:12) and joy over the gift despite age (24:36).
Fulfillment of the covenant promise: 24:36 shows that the promise in 17:19 was fulfilled.
Connects the event (24:36) to the naming and the joy (21:6) that follows from it.
Direct allusion: 9:9 quotes the prophecy that 24:36 confirms as fulfilled.
